questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$7200$ is charged interest at $15\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
How much lower is the balance at the end of the **second** month if the repayment is $\$600$ rather than $\$450$?
Round each month's interest to the nearest cent.

options.why: Counted the two extra repayments but ignored the interest saved in the second month.
Compared the balances after one month instead of after two.
Gave only the interest saved in month $2$, not the whole difference in the balances.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$260\,000$ can be repaid monthly at $\$1980$ over $25$ years, or fortnightly at $\$990$ over $21$ years.
What is the difference in the total amount repaid?

options.why: Gave the total repaid under the monthly option instead of the difference between the two.
Gave the interest paid under the fortnightly option rather than the difference in totals.
Used $24$ fortnights in a year instead of $26$.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$190\,000$ is repaid at $\$1300$ per month over $22$ years.
After $6$ years a lump sum of $\$25\,000$ is paid, and the loan is cleared after a further $154$ monthly repayments.
How much less is paid overall?

options.why: Left the lump sum out of the new total, so the $\$25\,000$ actually paid was not counted.
Gave the lump sum itself rather than the reduction in the total paid.
Counted only the $154$ repayments after the lump sum and left out the first $6$ years.

questions.solution_text:
Without the lump sum: total $= 1300 \times 12 \times 22$
$= \$343\,200$
With the lump sum:
Number of repayments $= 6 \times 12 + 154 = 226$
Total $= 1300 \times 226 + 25\,000$
$= 293\,800 + 25\,000$
$= \$318\,800$
Difference $= 343\,200 - 318\,800$
$= \$24\,400$

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$95\,000$ is due to be repaid at $\$760$ per month over $18$ years.
The borrower instead pays $\$850$ per month, clearing the loan in $15$ years and $2$ months.
How much is saved in total?

options.why: Gave the original total repaid instead of the saving.
Gave the extra paid each month rather than the saving over the whole loan.
Used exactly $15$ years ($180$ months) instead of $15$ years and $2$ months.
Read the term from the $\$675$ per month curve instead of the $\$1350$ curve.
Read where the balance is about half repaid instead of where it reaches zero.
Halved the $110$-month term, assuming doubling the repayment exactly halves the time.

questions.solution_text:
Follow the $\$1350$ per month curve down to the horizontal axis.
It meets the axis just past the $40$ mark.
To the nearest $10$ months, the loan takes about $40$ months.

questions.question_text: Why does an extra payment made early in a loan save more interest than the same extra payment made near the end of the loan?

options.text: The balance owing is larger early on, so the reduction avoids interest on a bigger balance for more of the remaining periods.
The interest rate charged is higher in the early years of a loan than in the later years.
options.why: The rate does not change; it is the balance the rate is applied to that changes.

options.text: The lender charges the same total interest either way, so only the term of the loan changes.
options.why: A lower balance is charged less interest each period, so the total interest changes too.

options.text: Early repayments are counted twice by the lender, once as interest and once as principal.
options.why: A repayment is counted once; part covers that period's interest and the rest reduces the balance.

questions.solution_text:
Interest each period is charged on the balance owing.
An extra payment made early removes that amount from the balance for every remaining period.
The same payment made near the end removes it for only a few periods, so it saves far less interest.

questions.question_text:
A borrower owes $\$126\,000$ on a loan charged at $8.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly and pays a lump sum of $\$18\,000$ off the balance.
By how much does the next month's interest charge fall?

options.why: Gave the interest charge before the lump sum rather than the fall in the charge.
Gave the interest charge after the lump sum rather than the fall in the charge.
Gave the lump sum itself instead of the interest it saves in one month.

questions.solution_text:
Rate per month $= \dfrac{0.084}{12} = 0.007$
Before: $I = 126\,000 \times 0.007 = \$882$
After: $I = 108\,000 \times 0.007 = \$756$
The interest charge falls by $882 - 756 = \$126$.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$330\,000$ is repaid at $\$2100$ per month over $30$ years.
After $12$ years the repayment is increased to $\$2600$ per month and the loan is repaid after a further $145$ months.
How much less is paid in total?

options.why: Gave the original total repaid instead of the reduction in the total.
Kept the original $\$2100$ repayment for the second stage instead of using $\$2600$.
Gave the increase in the monthly repayment rather than the saving over the whole loan.

questions.solution_text:
Without the increase: total $= 2100 \times 12 \times 30$
$= \$756\,000$
With the increase:
First $12$ years: $2100 \times 144 = \$302\,400$
Remaining $145$ months: $2600 \times 145 = \$377\,000$
Total $= 302\,400 + 377\,000 = \$679\,400$
Difference $= 756\,000 - 679\,400$
$= \$76\,600$
